title: Revision timer task and test table
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Programming 2: data structures, files and subprograms
source: Seeded from computing/y10 lesson 35 (Pupil PDF worksheet: revision timer task and test table)
intro: Lesson 35: Subprograms in practice: building a small program from functions. To understand how to decompose a problem into subprograms and build a working program from them

questions.q: Calculate by hand: zakah_due(12000, 5000) and zakah_due(5000, 5000).
Pupil PDF: build a 'revision timer' program from three functions: get_minutes(), split(minutes) returning hours and minutes, and show(h, m). Test it with 135 and 45.
questions.a: split uses // and %; 135 → 2 h 15 min; 45 → 0 h 45 min.
questions.model: The teacher writes split: def split(minutes): return minutes // 60, minutes % 60

questions.q: Extend: add a test table with three tests for split().
Stretch: design (in pseudo-code) the subprograms for a library-loan system.
questions.a: e.g. find_book(title), lend(book, pupil), return_book(book), overdue_list(date).

questions.q: Which test value checks the boundary of 'amount >= nisab'?
Back to our ponder: A big project is easier when each person builds one part. How is that like subprograms?
questions.a: Each subprogram is a part with a clear job; they fit together through parameters and return values.
